newsitem.title: PERU: Telefonica del Peru to issue 50 mln sol debt Thurs.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica del Peru to issue 50 mln sol debt Thurs.

text.p: Telefonica del Peru announced Tuesday it will auction Thursday 50 million soles ($19.4 million) worth of short-term debt as the first tranche of a planned $180 million issue.
At Thursday's auction, the company will offer four series of instruments with maturities of 30, 90, 180 and 270 days.
Telefonica said it has set a minimum price reference for the issue ranging from 98.8 percent for the 30-day series to 90.3 percent for the 270-day series.
Local rating agency Duff & Phelps del Peru has classifed the first tranche at its highest rating of DPp1+, according to the company.
Last week, the Lima Stocks and Securities Board (CONASEV) gave Telefonica approval to issue the $180 million over three years with instruments carrying a maximum maturity of one year.
The income from the issue will be used for expansion and repair work, according to company officials.
The company also recently began an issue over three years of 250 million soles of corporate bonds.
The firm is majority-owned by Spain's Telefonica de Espana after its $2.0 billion privatization in 1994.
